heading: San Francisco
description: A map of San Francisco with toggleable layers: the five parts of the city, 41 neighborhoods and SF Find's 117, known-as names, landmarks, historic and cultural districts, supervisor, Assembly, State Senate and congressional districts, main streets, freeways, BART, Muni Metro and the cable cars, and the trains of the nine-county Bay Area.
attribution: Neighborhoods, supervisor districts, historic and cultural districts, landmark buildings: City and County of San Francisco (DataSF) · Cities and counties of the Bay Area: MTC/ABAG · State Senate and Assembly districts, counties beyond the region & ACS figures: U.S. Census Bureau · Congressional districts (Proposition 50, AB 604): California Department of Technology · BART, Caltrain & Muni: GTFS from BART, Caltrain and SFMTA · SMART, ACE, Capitol Corridor & VTA lines, streets, highways & address search: © OpenStreetMap contributors via Nominatim · Skyscrapers: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA)

lens.label: Neighborhood lens
lens.source: American Community Survey 2020–2024 (U.S. Census Bureau), tracts summed into the 41 Analysis Neighborhoods.

lenses.note: Median home value and rent, weighted by owners and renters, ranked into thirds across San Francisco's 38 residential Analysis Neighborhoods. Survey estimates for 2020–2024, not current prices.

Typical transit trip to Montgomery Street station in the Financial District leaving 8–9 am on a weekday, walking to the stop included (Muni buses, Metro, streetcars and cable cars, BART and Caltrain). Median across each neighborhood.
lenses.source: Muni, BART and Caltrain schedules, routed with r5py.

hubs.name: Montgomery St
hubs.note: Typical transit trip to Montgomery Street station in the Financial District leaving 8–9 am on a weekday, walking to the stop included (Muni buses, Metro, streetcars and cable cars, BART and Caltrain). Median across each neighborhood.

hubs.name: 4th & King
hubs.note: Typical transit trip to 4th & King in Mission Bay (the Caltrain terminal and the T Third) leaving 8–9 am on a weekday, walking to the stop included (Muni buses, Metro, streetcars and cable cars, BART and Caltrain). Median across each neighborhood.

lenses.note: Share of commuters who drive: under 25%, 25–50%, 50% or more. Fewer San Franciscans drive to work than people anywhere else in the region, so the cuts are New York's.
Share of households that rent: under 35%, 35–60%, over 60%.

living.caveat: Survey estimates for 2020–2024, not current prices, for the whole neighborhood. Rent is what renting households pay, utilities included, counting rent-controlled and subsidized homes, so it sits well below what a new lease costs. Use them to compare neighborhoods, not to budget.
